text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.8% today after climbing nearly 16% over two weeks, largely reversing yesterday's sharp 4.6% gain. The pullback came as news broke that the Trump administration struck a deal to import Russian diesel into the U.S. market—a direct threat to domestic refiners' pricing power and margins. With diesel prices already elevated due to Middle East conflicts and refinery disruptions, an influx of cheaper Russian fuel undercuts the premium that companies like Marathon have been commanding.

The broader picture shows the refining sector caught between opposing forces: tightening fuel supplies (refineries running at 92.7% capacity, hurricane risks to Gulf operations, tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz limiting Middle Eastern exports) that normally support high prices, versus geopolitical moves that could flood the market with alternative supply. Yesterday's rally reflected optimism about tight markets; today's decline reflects trader skepticism that import deals will actually ease the supply crunch enough to justify maintaining current profit margins.
